nodes.rationale: A repeat inspection would need the same device, accounts and app versions. Re-rating recordings tests the judgments, which is where single-analyst walkthroughs are weakest (Mahatody et al.), at about a quarter of the cost. nodes.label: C18 Availability and limitations
nodes.change_summary: Availability lists the raw output of both models and the validation sample with selection probabilities and both coders' labels. nodes.rationale: Limitations must match the design actually used. Correlated errors are the main residual weakness of a two-model design, and the reader should hear it from the author.

nodes.label: C14 Reporting: two bounds, corrected estimates, RQ2 secondary analysis
nodes.change_summary: Every RQ1 proportion is given over applicable pathways and over applicable + uncertain. Routine-label figures are corrected estimates with intervals; high-stakes counts come with the estimated miss rate. RQ2 adds a pre-fixed secondary analysis of reassurance, generic-risk and responsibility wording without a named harm. "Other surface pairs" is removed (RQ4 narrowed). Absence statements cite measured recall.
nodes.norm_label: c14 reporting: two bounds, corrected estimates, rq2 secondary analysis
nodes.rationale: The instrument test found no named harm in a 9,427-word policy, so RQ2 could be empty; fixing the secondary analysis in advance keeps it from being a post-hoc rescue. Uncertain pathways need a stated rule or the denominator becomes a hidden choice.

nodes.label: C11 Interface-text coding aligned with the new design
nodes.change_summary: Interface units are coded by both models and checked like policy units, and they form their own validation stratum (V4). The walkthrough-output table says the same.
nodes.norm_label: c11 interface-text coding aligned with the new design
nodes.rationale: The old text referred to "validation apps" coded by hand, which no longer exists. Making interface units a stratum guarantees that interface recall is measured, instead of inferred from policies.

nodes.label: C17 Minimum feasible study made concrete
nodes.change_summary: Lists what is never cut (policy coding of all apps, high-stakes check, V5) and, highlighted, what is cut first (second walkthrough rating, then the interface stratum). The old "marketing collection is reduced first" is removed, since marketing is no longer collected.
nodes.norm_label: c17 minimum feasible study made concrete
nodes.rationale: A fallback order fixed before collection prevents later cuts from favouring convenient results.

nodes.label: C13 LLM subsection rewritten: two models, routing, label-hidden human check
nodes.change_summary: New title "LLM Coding with Two Models and Human Checks". Four paragraphs and a short routing table (Table 4.12): why models code (volume; 178 units in one policy); why the raw labels cannot be used directly (Egami et al.); two models of different families; the three stages with span checks kept; routine vs. high-stakes labels; the human check without the models' labels in view; raw output kept apart. The full rule-and-precedent table moves to Appendix B.1 and is updated.
nodes.norm_label: c13 llm subsection rewritten: two models, routing, label-hidden human check
nodes.rationale: You want the models to do the coding and no person to read all text. That makes three things essential: (1) a second model family, because LLM errors are correlated but not identical (Kim et al. 2025), so the union catches more of the rare harms; (2) people check only what carries RQ2/RQ3, and they check it blind, because showing LLM labels pulls human labels toward them and inflates measured accuracy (Schroeder et al. 2025; Wang et al. 2024); (3) agreement between the two models is called robustness, never reliability. The old "three runs, review every one-run label" rule is dropped from the main run: in the instrument test it sent about a quarter of labels to review.

nodes.label: C16 Validation rewritten: stratified sample of units, two coders, corrected estimates
nodes.change_summary: New title "Validation Sample, Agreement, and Error Estimates". Units, not apps; strata V1 model disagreement, V2 uncertain, V3 harm vocabulary without a high-stakes label (absorbs the missed-mention audit), V4 interface, V5 plain random; known selection probabilities. Author and second coder code the sample blind; Krippendorff's α with .800/.667 rules; span-overlap scoring; weighted precision/recall; corrected estimates (Egami et al.; Angelopoulos et al.); absence claims tied to recall, "not estimable" below 20 positives. Highlighted proposals: ≥500 units with ≥150 in V5; routine codes with precision lower bound < 0.80 only as estimates; supervisor fallback codes V1–V2.
nodes.norm_label: c16 validation rewritten: stratified sample of units, two coders, corrected estimates
nodes.rationale: Ten random apps would very likely yield fewer than 20 positives for every harm and stance code (Clue: 0 in 178 units), so the old rule would have fired for exactly the codes the RQs depend on and forced full manual reading. Sampling units, oversampling where errors hide, and weighting back gives estimates for the whole corpus with valid intervals. The numbers are proposals until the pilot shows the coding time per unit, so they carry \highlight/\todo marks.

nodes.norm_label: c19 unchanged on purpose: literature review procedure, harm concepts, generic model
nodes.rationale: The review found no methodological problem in these parts, and rewriting sound text adds risk without benefit.

occurrences.evidence_and_scope: Article pp.669–671; SM TheoremS1 pp.7–8; finite-population section/TheoremS5/CorollaryS14 pp.21–22; PDF pp.1,2,3,13,14,27,28. The published article requires an estimand-specific rectifier, then combines predicted-data fit and gold-label residual error. The supplement includes finite-population results for a uniformly sampled labelled subset, including mean inference. It does not directly establish this thesis unequal-probability overlapping-strata, clustered unit-to-pathway design or arbitrary nonlinear aggregation. The inventory Gligoric candidate is not this source and was discarded.
occurrences.remedy: Cite the actual Science article and relevant supplement; define a rectifier/estimator and compatible gold-sampling variance before claiming interval validity. Acknowledge that finite-population inference exists, while justifying any unequal-probability extension.

nodes.label: R1. Define the quantities and estimator at the level actually reported
nodes.norm_label: r1. define the quantities and estimator at the level actually reported
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential design repair. Chapter lines 1803–1809, 1845–1857, 1938–1963 and 1995–2002.**

The validation observes paragraph/interface-block labels, while the reported outcomes include whether an app mentions anything and the highest coverage level reached anywhere on a pathway. These are nonlinear aggregates. Ten repeated mentions in one app and one mention in each of ten apps can have the same unit total and different app counts. Correcting the unit total does not identify the latter.

Make an analysis specification with one row per primary outcome: target corpus, observational/weighting unit, numerator, denominator, aggregation, fixed model prediction and uncertainty source. Name and implement the estimator, including how uncertain model labels are encoded. For additive unit totals, a probability-weighted difference estimator is a plausible option. For app/pathway existence or maxima, justify an estimator for that aggregate or add probability-sampled complete app/surface or app–code audits. A feasible alternative is to keep corrected unit estimates and label app/pathway detection summaries with their actual evidential limits.

Egami and Angelopoulos support principled correction under stated designs and assumptions; neither citation establishes this study’s new aggregation, unequal-probability audit or provider-resampling procedure. Check the implemented estimator on small constructed corpora with repeated and singleton mentions, correlated errors and unequal inclusion. This needs implementation and evidence, not another assurance sentence.

nodes.label: R2. Make the validation frames, inclusion probabilities and uncertainty executable
nodes.norm_label: r2. make the validation frames, inclusion probabilities and uncertainty executable
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential design repair. Lines 1897–1900, 1931–1933 and 1944–1993.**

V1–V4 overlap: an uncertain interface unit can also be a disagreement unit. Define either a mutually exclusive precedence partition or a multiple-frame draw with exact union inclusion probabilities and duplicate handling. Specify small/exhausted-stratum rules and freeze the vocabulary/allocation before drawing.

Development/test/pilot units remain in the corpus but have zero validation inclusion. A design-based correction for the entire corpus cannot silently extrapolate to them. Give them an independently checked census contribution, or state a narrower independent target and report development material separately. Development coding must not count as independent model evaluation.

State whether intervals describe audit uncertainty within this fixed selected corpus or a wider population. The app sample is purposive/feedback-prioritised, so these intervals do not provide German-market sampling representativeness. Use a variance procedure that respects the actual validation design and relevant shared-document/provider dependence. Provider bootstrapping alone is not a derivation of validity.

nodes.label: R3. Separate a mention from its polarity and from pathway-specific coverage
nodes.norm_label: r3. separate a mention from its polarity and from pathway-specific coverage
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential measurement repair. Lines 99–108, 1667–1679 and 1803–1818.**

An explicit statement that a harm is impossible is still a mention. Recording denial elsewhere does not make it correct for a coverage scale to call it silent. Keep polarity-neutral mention/coverage separately from acknowledgment, prevention and denial; if affirmative-risk coverage is desired, name it separately.

Likewise, one psychological or economic harm mention cannot automatically cover every pathway in that category. Match the consequence and relevant data/actor/context to the pathway. Keep a separate coarse category-mention indicator if it is useful. Check a constructed case where one category has two different actors/pathways and only one is described. These are operational choices to record under D9/D12 before rewriting the method.

nodes.label: R4. Resolve OR+ sufficiency and actor access
nodes.norm_label: r4. resolve or+ sufficiency and actor access
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential model repair. Lines 884–885 and 1793–1797; reference-model K10/P13/P16.**

“More than one may be needed” cannot become “any single input suffices” solely because the study asks about possibility rather than likelihood. K10 currently makes this an active issue. Explicitly encode supported sufficient combinations as an OR of ANDs, or retain uncertainty where the source does not identify the combination. Ordinary OR is justified only if each listed alternative is sufficient in the named actor/context.

An on-device data item does not by itself give a provider, advertiser or other recipient the ability to use it. Make actor access/conditions explicit. Run the evaluator and affected examples again after the rule is chosen. The independent pathway check should examine those contextual prerequisites, not only whether a paper uses a similar harm term.

nodes.label: R5. Bring the current instrument bundle into agreement with the chapter
nodes.norm_label: r5. bring the current instrument bundle into agreement with the chapter
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential reproducibility repair. Chapter lines 1935–2013; codebook v5 lines 274–300; study navigation and current prompts.**

The chapter has moved to two models, sampled units, alpha and corrected estimates, but current instruments still contain the earlier ten-app/one-model workflow and old acceptance/escalation rules. Version the revised codebook, prompts/schemas, blind human sheets, validation-sampling manifest and app-decision forms. Preserve older versions as historical, as required by the project workflow.

RQ2’s new responsibility wording without named harm also needs a separate operational code; the existing named-harm stance rule does not automatically collect it. Update the authoritative instrument manifest and navigation so a second person can execute the same procedure. Then run that actual bundle in the real pilot.

nodes.label: R6. Confirm second-coder capacity and use the pilot to choose a feasible plan
nodes.norm_label: r6. confirm second-coder capacity and use the pilot to choose a feasible plan
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential execution decision. Lines 1381–1387, 1921–1933, 1961–1984 and 2031–2036; D8–D10.**

The same second person is expected to code validation units, check trees/app judgments and rate recordings. Their identity and capacity remain open. Confirm the person, training, tasks and time budget. Measure actual capture, transcript checking, coding, adjudication and model cost in the five-app pilot; account for the planned two-week recoding interval.

A supervisor coding V1/V2 only is a different validation design: it does not establish the same human reliability across blind-spot and interface strata. If capacity is limited, choose a smaller probability sample double-coded across the relevant strata and narrow claims accordingly, rather than treating selective disagreement-only coding as equivalent.

The proposed 500-unit total, 150-unit residual allocation, 20-positive reporting rule, precision bound and 10% sensitivity threshold are choices awaiting feasibility/precision justification. This review does not declare them numerically adequate or inadequate without prevalence/workload evidence. Do not change codes on the validation set and then call that same set untouched confirmation.

nodes.label: R7. Count remaining misses across all relevant strata and retain human uncertainty
nodes.norm_label: r7. count remaining misses across all relevant strata and retain human uncertainty
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: essential analysis clarification. Lines 1735–1739, 1951–1963 and 2000–2012.**

Both models can miss a harm in a unit sampled because of a routine-code disagreement or an interface stratum. V3/V5 alone do not necessarily exhaust joint misses. Use all appropriate probability-sampled units to estimate misses with their weights. A human check can also be wrong; distinguish single-human reviewed findings from independently double-coded/adjudicated reference labels.

Report weighted precision/recall with observed denominators, prevalence and uncertainty by code/surface. A small number of positives or zero observed misses cannot certify an individual app’s silence. Keep “not found in the captured material” language where absence cannot be supported. Specify alpha’s coding representation/metric, weighting and undefined/rare-code handling; Krippendorff’s thresholds are cautious guidelines, not proof of truth.

nodes.label: R8. Specify applicability scenarios, numerators and the primary weighting unit
nodes.norm_label: r8. specify applicability scenarios, numerators and the primary weighting unit
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: required before reporting. Lines 1782–1799 and 1845–1857.**

The dual applicable-only/applicable-plus-uncertain calculation is useful, but both numerators and denominators must be stated. Adding uncertain cases to a denominator is not automatically a valid lower/upper identification bound. Call them sensitivity scenarios unless bounds are derived. Choose equal app/provider weighting or explicit pathway weighting, and explain the alternative. Show source/assumption-dependent applicability so a more transparent provider is not silently penalised for revealing more pathways.

There is also a concrete counting inconsistency to check: line 1256 refers to “50 selected providers,” while the results describe 47 ranked providers plus Apple and Samsung, with two Apple apps (results lines 429–431, 520–522). The threshold denominator must distinguish 50 apps, 49 providers and the 47 ranked providers; the current sensitivity table uses the latter. This is an arithmetic/unit clarification, not a new sampling result.

nodes.label: R9. Freeze executable walkthrough and bilingual rules
nodes.norm_label: r9. freeze executable walkthrough and bilingual rules
nodes.rationale:
**Priority: required for retained interface findings. Lines 1386–1447, 1474–1579 and 1342–1355; D7/D10/D17.**

Fix platform/device/OS, account and reset states, permission/consent profile, route preparation, stopping/time rules, synthetic inputs and subgoal success criteria. Account deletion, data deletion and portability are distinct outcomes; preserve partial completion rather than one ambiguous “success.” The model’s in-app-only incapability condition must agree with the protocol’s treatment of a usable external route.

For English-first collection, verify that the selected document applies to the German/EEA user and app. Arora’s semi-parallel US/German policies are evidence that versions can differ, not interchangeable translations. Compare language counterparts in matched account/consent/task states before destructive changes, record which pairs were inspected, and define how a material difference triggers additional coding during main collection. Until then the log documents observed differences; it does not measure all effects of language choice.

Specify the lay task scenario and assumed privacy knowledge. Re-rating recordings assesses interpretation of recorded routes, not independent discovery of omitted routes. Keep that distinction and the explicit absence of a user study.

nodes.label: W1 — A harm category mention is not coverage of every causal pathway in that category
nodes.norm_label: w1 — a harm category mention is not coverage of every causal pathway in that category
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Major. Confidence: high, based on the chapter's own definitions and verified primary-source context requirements.

Evidence anchor: text: methodology L1803–1809, "A named harm counts for the pathways of its category." Related anchors: codebook L248; methodology L917–920; model P05–P08 (L65–68).

The same category contains materially different harms and actors. A warning about distress after account theft can currently give harm-level coverage to partner harassment and fear of legal proceedings, because all are H-PSY. Even perfect unit coding cannot justify that attribution. The codebook instead says a mention must concern the pathway's data. Knabenhans §4 PDF p. 6 makes the recipient and the semantics of disclosed data necessary to identify harms; Appendix A is a taxonomy, not a rule that its members are interchangeable.

Minimum repair: keep category mention as a separate summary. Credit pathway coverage only where the text establishes the relevant consequence and compatible data/actor/access scope; explicitly allow a category-only or scope-unclear mention without spreading it to all pathways. Preserve the existing node/data requirement and extend it to consequence/actor matching where relevant.

Evidence needed before submission: independently checked mappings for broad warnings and warnings naming one psychological consequence, with a crosswalk showing why each received pathway credit. Include a counterexample where one H-PSY pathway is covered and another is not.

nodes.label: W2 — Excluding denials from coverage conflates communication with acknowledgement
nodes.norm_label: w2 — excluding denials from coverage conflates communication with acknowledgement
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Major. Confidence: high; internal construct mismatch.

Evidence anchor: text: methodology L1806–1807, "A denied node is reported as denied and does not count as coverage." Related anchors: RQ1 L99–101; RQ2 L102–103; Axis A L1667–1669; codebook S-DEN L177.

A provider that explicitly says a harm is impossible has communicated that harm. Under the current rule it may receive the same coverage level as a provider that never names it, despite denial being one of the intended stance findings. Reporting the denial elsewhere helps, but does not make a "missing harm" or silence interpretation of that coverage variable correct. This is especially important for the research question about harms providers acknowledge or downplay.

Minimum repair: derive explicit mention independently of assertion status. Report acknowledged/possible mentions and denied/prevented mentions separately, while retaining all mentioned nodes. If the author deliberately wants an acknowledgement-only measure, name it accordingly and never equate its complement with silence or unmentioned harms. No need to redefine every denial as acknowledgement.

Evidence needed: constructed and then pilot-tested cases for silence, possible harm, outright denial, and a protection claim that prevents a named harm. The reported tables must preserve those distinctions.

nodes.label: W3 — OR+ conversion and actor-free inference can make applicability too permissive
nodes.norm_label: w3 — or+ conversion and actor-free inference can make applicability too permissive
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Major. Confidence: high on the logical conversion; moderate on which concrete tracker combinations should suffice.

Evidence anchor: text: methodology L1793–1796, "OR+ is read like OR". Related anchors: L884–885; model K10 L42; model P13/P16 L76/L82; codebook L72–73.

The chapter first correctly says OR+ can need several components, then evaluates it as if any single component suffices. Asking about possibility does not establish that an incomplete combination is sufficient. The checked source explicitly uses OR+ when more than one component might be needed (Knabenhans §4.1 PDF p. 6).

The current model exposes a concrete consequence: K10 is `orplus: [IM4, IM7, CO2]`. CO2 alone describes predictions or scores computed for the user, including potentially local predictions. It does not establish that either named actor (provider or advertising partner) receives the relevant attributes. Yet it can mark K10, and consequently manipulation/profile-based-price pathways, present. This conflicts with the chapter's own warning that a user-facing prediction does not establish third-party access. Knabenhans §5.1 PDF p. 11 defines distinguishing through the recipient's presentation of information; it does not supply that missing access condition for trackers.

Minimum repair: replace executable OR+ with explicitly justified sufficient combinations, or keep it uncertain until the combination is evidenced. Split actors where their required access differs. A local insight can be coded as a benign capability mention without automatically establishing a provider/advertiser's harmful capability. This does not require probabilistic risk assessment or a new domain sample.

Evidence needed: the independent pathway audit already promised at L1927–1929 must check actor/data/access sufficiency, not just whether a cited paper contains the harm label. Include an on-device-only tracker and a tracker with documented advertising disclosure as boundary cases; verify the two receive different applicability states where warranted.

nodes.label: W4 — The operational export/deletion leaf contradicts the chapter's correction for alternative routes
nodes.norm_label: w4 — the operational export/deletion leaf contradicts the chapter's correction for alternative routes
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Major for I2-based autonomy findings unless fixed before use. Confidence: high; direct instrument inconsistency.

Evidence anchor: text: model L26, "no working in-app way to delete or export the data." Related anchors: I2 L44; P10 L73; methodology L1560–1563.

IM12 can be true when there is no working in-app control, even if the provider offers a usable request route. The chapter expressly says that the missing button cannot establish I2 because another route or provider-mediated request may exist. That distinction matters: missing an in-app control measures findability or control modality, while inability to leave without losing data is the incapability that supports the autonomy/lock-in consequence.

Minimum repair: separate an absent in-app control from absence of a usable route. Set I2 from the latter, treating unexamined routes as uncertain; retain the first for walkthrough reporting. Distinguish export from deletion where one exists and the other does not.

Evidence needed: a recorded pilot case with an external request route, a case with explicit unsupported export/deletion, and coding showing no lock-in inference from a button non-finding alone. This is a fix to the existing model, not a requirement to test backend deletion effectiveness.

nodes.label: W5 — The universal-model phrasing and some origins exceed the stated evidence
nodes.norm_label: w5 — the universal-model phrasing and some origins exceed the stated evidence
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Minor. Confidence: high on wording, moderate on individual origin assignments.

Evidence anchor: text: methodology L628–629, "every function a health tracker can have"; D12 L15, "No completeness is claimed". Related anchors: methodology L35–36/L576–577 and L2079–2081; model CO2/CX3 L10/L14; codebook L51–54.

The bounded literature-derived model is defensible, but "every function" and "a real app is a subset" assert exhaustiveness. Later limitations cannot establish that. Origin assignments also need the stated functional boundary: derived insights are not indispensable to every tracker, and availability of an advertising/push identifier is not inherently unavoidable merely because a phone can expose it. The codebook itself recognizes this. Knabenhans' black/blue/red argument concerns a specified ideal functionality and deployment context, not any instance of an app capability.

Minimum repair: describe a reference model of functions evidenced within the study's scope. Define origins relative to the relevant function/use case and record the assumption; retain "argued" status. Do not infer that a provider cannot address an identifier simply from its context colour. Existing per-claim control assessment can remain.

Evidence needed: reviewer reasons for core/context/implementation origin decisions, including local insight and optional identifier examples. No proof of completeness is needed if no completeness claim is made.

nodes.label: W6 — Downplaying remains a deliberately narrow, study-defined construct
nodes.norm_label: w6 — downplaying remains a deliberately narrow, study-defined construct
nodes.rationale:
Severity: Minor. Confidence: high on source scope; moderate on expected pilot effect.

Evidence anchor: text: codebook L175, "a stated reason makes it `S-QUA`"; methodology L1672–1679 and L1857–1860.

Zou is a good precedent for inspecting wording, but not a validated source for this entire five-label taxonomy. Its pp. 7/10 explicitly discuss "no evidence" explanations as capable of downplaying risk even when factually accurate, and p. 9 disclaims direct evidence of consumer effects. The codebook's rule that any stated reason makes a dismissal qualification can exclude precisely such language from S-MIN. Requiring a named harm is a defensible scope choice, but it excludes much general risk reassurance; the new secondary analysis helps, though generic responsibility wording still needs an explicit coding rule.

Minimum repair: state that the five stance labels are the study's adaptation and that S-MIN measures unsupported explicit dismissal, if that narrow construct is intended. Add a rule and examples for no-evidence language, reasoned dismissal, generic reassurance and generic responsibility wording. Do not claim measured psychological downplaying or intent. Broader stance coding is optional, not a requirement for this study to be useful.

Evidence needed: pilot disagreements and resolutions on these boundaries, with negative examples and independent coding. Keep secondary language findings separate from harm-specific stance rates.

nodes.label: CLI, importable collect function and offline reparse
nodes.description: CLI writes JSON file or stdout, progress to stderr. Import collect from app_store_search with v001 on Python import path. --api-only skips pages. --reparse verifies hashes and rebuilds page fields offline, recording source JSON and parser hashes; also recovers interrupted checkpoints if every pending response was archived.
nodes.norm_label: cli, importable collect function and offline reparse

nodes.label: Request pacing and retry behavior
nodes.description: Documentation records approximately 20 API calls/minute; client spaces API requests 3.2 seconds and page requests one second across workers. Retries transient failures, honors Retry-After up to 60 seconds and reports longer requested waits.

nodes.label: Fitness candidate-discovery run
nodes.description: Example starts fitness, writing 05_Data/raw/appstore/fitness.json and archiving response evidence. Defaults Germany, requested English, limit 200 and page enrichment. Does not freeze a sample.

nodes.label: Raw evidence, provenance and snapshot protection
nodes.description: Existing snapshots protected against overwrite. Raw response bodies and HTTP metadata preserve attempts, dates, URLs and SHA-256 hashes. Absolute archive paths need explicit updates if moved; raw study files ignored by Git require backup.
nodes.norm_label: raw evidence, provenance and snapshot protection
nodes.rationale: Retain original response evidence and permit hash-verified reprocessing when page parsing changes.

nodes.label: Product-page identity and storefront verification
nodes.description: Final URL, canonical URL when present and embedded page intent must match requested country and app identity. No silent storefront switch. English requested; actual HTML language retained, observed Germany redirect l=en to l=en-GB.

nodes.label: Complete API metadata retention
nodes.description: Identity, bundle/app IDs, developer/seller, description, classification, language/age, pricing, ratings, version/release metadata, device support, minimum iOS/file size, screenshots/artwork URLs, plus raw_api_data including unknown fields. Media not downloaded.

nodes.label: Checkpointing and explicit partial collection status
nodes.description: JSON checkpointed as pages finish. Exit 0 completed, 1 collection/input failure, 2 saved results with page errors. Failed page retains app and API fields; collecting means interrupted checkpoint. Missing values null or empty lists. Atomic checkpoint saves retry transient Windows file locks; offline reparse can recover an interrupted checkpoint when every pending app response was archived successfully.
nodes.norm_label: checkpointing and explicit partial collection status

nodes.label: Interrupted checkpoint recovery and Windows lock retries
nodes.description: Offline reparse can recover an interrupted checkpoint only if every pending app response was archived successfully. Atomic checkpoint saves retry transient Windows file locks.
nodes.norm_label: interrupted checkpoint recovery and windows lock retries

nodes.label: API position is not verified native store search rank
nodes.description: Original order retained without sorting by ratings; requested and actual counts recorded. API result position is not independently verified iPhone store rank, German popularity or downloads. Responses can vary over time.
nodes.norm_label: api position is not verified native store search rank
nodes.rationale: Avoid claiming complete coverage or equivalence between API results and native storefront ranking.

nodes.label: Thesis eligibility remains unresolved by collector
nodes.description: Paid apps, native apps and apps without extracted policy links remain candidates. Script does not infer eligibility, invent downloads, select rating floor or freeze sample.
nodes.norm_label: thesis eligibility remains unresolved by collector

nodes.label: v001 full iPhone App Store keyword collector
nodes.description: Preserved full collector at scripts/appstore-scraper/v001/app_store_search.py. Retains every API field and enriches confirmed iPhone-compatible apps from public product pages. Python 3.10+, standard library, no API key.
nodes.norm_label: v001 full iphone app store keyword collector

nodes.label: Privacy disclosures and missing-link interpretation
nodes.description: Privacy labels are developer declarations, not independently tested behavior. Missing policy URL means parser did not find one in supported fields; it does not prove no policy exists. Linked policies and sites are not fetched.
nodes.rationale: Avoid converting listing declarations or extraction gaps into unsupported findings about app behavior or policy absence.

nodes.label: Public product-page enrichment
nodes.description: Public offer flags and subtitle, privacy/external links, privacy labels and details, purchase/subscription titles and prices, version history, compatibility/languages/provider details, page ratings and embedded reviews, JSON-LD and primary page content. Reviews are not exhaustive.

nodes.label: Embedded serialized-server-data parser
nodes.description: Public page structure is unversioned and can change. Explicit errors plus archived HTML support later reprocessing. No app download, login, device interaction or permission inspection.

nodes.label: Apple public iTunes Search API
nodes.description: Search parameters media=software, entity=software, country=de, lang=en_us, explicit=Yes. Requested limit 1-200. No documented pagination here; fewer returned results do not establish complete keyword coverage.

nodes.label: Primary-app data scope and raw-page preservation
nodes.description: product_page_data preserves primary product content including available accessibility/screenshots/shelves, omits analytics and related-app recommendations; original raw HTML preserves page evidence.
nodes.norm_label: primary-app data scope and raw-page preservation

nodes.label: Explicit iPhone support filter and preserved exclusions
nodes.description: supportedDevices must explicitly include iPhone. iPad-only, unknown compatibility, invalid records and duplicate IDs go to excluded_results with full API records and positions. This is a technical filter, not thesis eligibility.
nodes.norm_label: explicit iphone support filter and preserved exclusions

nodes.label: Offline collector verification coverage
nodes.description: unittest checks identity/storefront mismatches, unknown fields, missing values, iPhone filtering, API order, purchase/privacy/history extraction, page failures without losing candidates, HTTP retries, Windows file locks, checkpoint recovery and hash-verified offline reprocessing. Project checker also documented.

nodes.label: Competing explanations and normative inference ceiling
nodes.norm_label: competing explanations and normative inference ceiling

nodes.norm_label: current safeguards defeat blanket redesign demands
nodes.rationale: No critical unrepairable flaw is established. Bounded non-findings, uncertain states, no-security/no-intent claims and source checking already mitigate easy attacks; user studies and technical audits would expand scope.

nodes.norm_label: m1 category membership is not pathway-specific communication

nodes.label: W1. The promised empirical contribution has not yet been delivered
nodes.norm_label: w1. the promised empirical contribution has not yet been delivered
nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Major — a final-submission readiness blocker, not evidence that the proposed method is unsound.

**Evidence Anchor:** text: `03_Thesis/chapters/05_results.tex:794`, "Not answered: the only interface in the test is invented"; `:800–807`, "To be written."; `03_Thesis/chapters/07_conclusion.tex:4–8`, "To be written."

**Confidence:** High — directly stated manuscript status; no claim about unreported work outside the reviewed material.

The current results establish sampling, construction of the reference model and operation of a preliminary pipeline. They do not yet answer the four questions for the intended empirical sample. A polished methodology alone cannot support the advertised final thesis contribution.

**Minimum final-submission remedy:** perform and report the agreed real collection, pilot/freeze, coding and validation necessary for the retained questions; then write results, discussion and conclusion from those observations. If the intended contribution is deliberately narrowed, document the author/supervisor decision and revise the RQs and claims accordingly. Keep synthetic test records clearly separated from empirical evidence. Do not invent outcome values or fill result sections from expectations.

nodes.label: W2. The minimum viable study remains conditional on unconfirmed resources
nodes.norm_label: w2. the minimum viable study remains conditional on unconfirmed resources
nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Major.

**Evidence Anchor:** text: `03_Thesis/chapters/04_methodology.tex:1961–1964`, "The sample holds at least 500 units"; `:1982–1984`, "Who is the second coder?"; `:2033–2036`, "If time runs short".

**Confidence:** High about the dependency; moderate about total workload because no real pilot timings, staffing commitment or deadline were supplied.

The same second person is expected to double-code the validation sample, check reference pathways and judged decisions, and rate recorded walkthroughs. Fifty inspections with seven tasks, language counterparts, transcription checks and human review add substantial work around the automated coding. The proposed fallback covers V1 and V2 only, whereas the main procedure describes independent coding of the whole validation sample. That is a different level of evidence, not simply fewer hours. The proposed reduction of the interface stratum could also narrow the support for RQ4.

**Minimum final-submission remedy:** use the real five-app pilot to record actual effort and cost, confirm the second person's availability and tasks, and adopt a feasible collection/validation plan before main coding. Record the resulting scope in the decision log. If a fallback is used, explicitly state which independence, reliability and surface-specific claims remain supportable. The planned two-week intra-coder interval must also fit the actual schedule. This finding does not require hiring extra researchers or adding inspections.

nodes.norm_label: w3. the evidence supporting the reference yardstick and research gap is unfinished
nodes.rationale:

**Evidence Anchor:** text: `03_Thesis/chapters/04_methodology.tex:501–502`, "Check every decision"; `03_Thesis/chapters/05_results.tex:8–10`, "currently inconsistent with it."; `:168–169`, "the university library was not tried."

**Confidence:** High — explicit unresolved checks in the current manuscript and D14 register entry.

The literature is foundational here: it supports both the claimed gap and the pathways against which omissions are judged. The results still report superseded search routes/rules, screening decisions await author checking, and retrieval has not reached the stopping rule the current method specifies. The second-person source check of the trees is also still proposed. A structured pipeline does not substitute for settling this evidence base.

**Minimum final-submission remedy:** reconcile the retained corpus and search/screening results with the adopted D14 procedure, complete the stated retrieval attempts or record the justified terminal status for unresolved records, and check the screening/extraction decisions that support the trees and gap. Complete and report the promised source review of the pathways before freezing the yardstick. Verify or remove the unread De and Le Métayer 2017 method claim flagged at methodology lines 640–642. State the contribution as an evidenced, bounded extension of preceding work; a claim that no similar study exists is unnecessary.

nodes.label: M1 — The corrected estimator does not yet identify the main outcomes (major; first priority)
nodes.norm_label: m1 — the corrected estimator does not yet identify the main outcomes (major; first priority)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1601–1602` counts unit/code labels; `1803–1809` defines coverage as the highest level anywhere on an app/pathway/surface; `1845–1857` reports applicable app/pathway counts and coverage categories; `1995–2002` promises corrected figures and valid intervals from a sample of units. The named procedure, equation, target population, treatment of uncertain predictions, and correction for nonlinear aggregation are absent.

**Why it matters:** an app with ten mentions of a capability and an app with one mention each count once for presence. An estimated correction to the number of positive paragraphs can estimate a unit total; it cannot simply be converted into the number of apps mentioning the capability or the number of pathways whose maximum level is two. Correlated mistakes within a policy make this distinction consequential. Provider-resampling does not repair an unidentified target/estimator.

**Minimum fix:** enumerate the estimands in a short analysis table: observational unit, target corpus, numerator, denominator, aggregation function and uncertainty source. Choose a concrete design-based difference estimator for additive unit totals (for fixed predictions g, a finite-corpus mean can use the full-corpus prediction mean plus the probability-weighted sample mean of y−g). State how uncertain labels enter g. For app/pathway maxima, either (a) add probability-sampled complete app/surface or app/pathway audits sufficient to observe their true aggregated outcome, or (b) supply and justify a specific estimator using the joint-inclusion information needed by that nonlinear target. Report uncorrected detection summaries explicitly as such if neither is feasible. Treat this as a choice, not a demand to manually read every app.

**Needs actual work:** estimator implementation; small simulated corpora with repeated mentions, within-provider dependence, false positives/negatives and unequal sampling; verification that the claimed interval targets the declared quantity. Wording alone cannot establish validity. Egami et al., §4, specifies a concrete pseudo-outcome and cross-fitting procedure; Angelopoulos et al. starts by choosing the estimand and its rectifier. Neither citation itself supplies this study's aggregation rule ([Egami et al.](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/d862f7f5445255090de13b825b880d59-Paper-Conference.pdf), [Angelopoulos et al.](https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~john/papers/AngelopoulosScience2023.pdf)).

nodes.label: M2 — Positivity, overlapping strata and interval design need a single executable sampling specification (major)
nodes.norm_label: m2 — positivity, overlapping strata and interval design need a single executable sampling specification (major)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1897–1900` and `1931–1933` retain test/pilot apps while excluding their units from validation; `1944–1963` excludes prompt-development units, lists overlapping V1–V4 conditions, and says probabilities are known for the whole corpus. A disagreeing, uncertain interface unit can satisfy three strata. No precedence or multiple-frame selection formula is stated. `1990` only says intervals resample providers.

**Why it matters:** development units have zero gold-sample inclusion in the stated target corpus. Their residual error cannot be corrected design-wise by weighting the rest. For other units, inclusion probabilities depend on whether the five categories are a partition or overlapping draws. Naive provider bootstrap can also fail to reproduce a stratified unequal-probability audit; the sample of providers is not a random sample of all health-tracker providers.

**Minimum fix:** define a mutually exclusive priority partition or a documented multi-frame draw with deduplication and exact union-inclusion probabilities. Freeze vocabulary and allocation rules before drawing, including rules for small/exhausted strata. Separate development apps as a fully human-coded census contribution, or narrow the corrected target to the independent corpus and report development apps separately. Avoid using development coding to claim independent model performance. Define whether intervals describe gold-audit uncertainty within this fixed corpus or a wider superpopulation, then choose a survey/design-respecting variance procedure with provider/document clustering where relevant. Do not interpret these intervals as German-market sampling uncertainty.

**Needs actual work:** a sampler that records frame membership, stratum, seed and inclusion probabilities, checks all target units have nonzero support (or a census gold outcome), and produces reproducible draws and appropriate replicate weights/variance. Egami et al., Assumption 1, requires known, positive gold-label probabilities; the paper's guarantee is asymptotic and conditional on its assumptions ([primary paper](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/d862f7f5445255090de13b825b880d59-Paper-Conference.pdf)).

nodes.label: M3 — Rare-label detection and high-stakes counts are less secure than the text claims (major)
nodes.norm_label: m3 — rare-label detection and high-stakes counts are less secure than the text claims (major)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1735–1739` checks returned high-stakes labels; `1951–1963` proposes vocabulary enrichment plus 150 residual units; `2000–2007` says remaining error is only joint model misses and V3/V5 estimate it; `2008–2012` gates interface claims and some routine counts. The preliminary policy contains no harm mentions (`1941–1942`), but no observed pilot prevalence or workload exists here.

**Why it matters:** human checking can still mislabel returned candidates. Jointly missed high-stakes labels may occur in V1/V2/V4 too, for example a paragraph that disagrees only about a routine code while both models miss a harm. If V5 is the residual partition, it represents only that residual. Raw positive counts plus an overall missed-mention fraction do not correct app-level absence or rare harm/stance combinations. Twenty positives is a reporting convention, not a guarantee of useful precision; zero positives is particularly uninformative about rare misses.

**Minimum fix:** estimate missed positives using all probability-sampled strata and report actual observed numerator/denominator counts, weights and uncertainty. Distinguish single-human checked findings from settled double-coded reference findings. Define rare-code outputs prospectively: no corpus absence conclusion when precision/recall cannot be usefully bounded; retain bounded detection language and qualitative examples. Predefine a feasible precision or interval-width target for principal codes and an escalation or reduced-scope rule if pilot evidence cannot support it. Clarify that an overall unit-level recall does not certify that a particular app contains no mention.

**Needs actual work:** real pilot prevalence and time measurements, then independent gold labels and code/surface-specific error bounds. The proposed 500/150 allocation cannot currently be called adequate or inadequate numerically; its adequacy has not been demonstrated.

nodes.label: M4 — The second-coder fallback does not preserve the principal validation design (major)
nodes.norm_label: m4 — the second-coder fallback does not preserve the principal validation design (major)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1966–1984` calls every validation unit independently double-coded but permits supervisor coding of V1/V2 only. `1927–1929` also requires this person to check every tree pathway, `1381–1387` adds ten walkthrough re-ratings, and `2031–2036` leaves effort and reduction rules to the pilot. D8:15–16 confirms identity remains open and the V1/V2 fallback. `2000–2002` nevertheless treats human-checked labels as leaving only model misses.

**Why it matters:** the fallback leaves blind-spot, vocabulary and some interface units with one reference coder. It cannot establish human reliability across the corpus or the same quality of gold correction as the main design. Unit sampling may expose many or nearly all apps, so “decisions of the sampled apps” (`1982–1983`) is not a bounded app-review workload.

**Minimum fix:** before freeze, confirm a named coder, availability and actual coding budget; separate the workload for text units, source-checking pathways, app-level decisions and walkthrough ratings. Specify a scientifically coherent reduced design if the coder is unavailable: e.g., a smaller probability sample double-coded across all relevant strata, with narrower claims, rather than only difficult/disagreement units. State clearly which reference labels remain single-coded if that route is chosen. Define a sample of app-level decisions including positive and negative mismatch judgments, not just “sampled apps”.

**Needs actual work:** coder recruitment, training/calibration separate from evaluation, timed pilot double-coding and subsequent independent coding. A supervisor decision and available labour are required; prose cannot replace them.

nodes.label: M5 — Current instruments implement the earlier design (major for reproducibility; straightforward pre-freeze repair)
nodes.norm_label: m5 — current instruments implement the earlier design (major for reproducibility; straightforward pre-freeze repair)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** codebook v5:274–300 still prescribes ten whole validation apps, Cohen's κ/AC1, two recoded apps, a separate exhaustive lexical sweep and full-manual-review triggers; thesis `1938–2013` now prescribes sampled units, two models, α and estimated correction. Walkthrough protocol v7:189–195 still references the old manual-decision/second-inspection route. Study README:6 points to codebook v4 and walkthrough v3. D9:22 explicitly supersedes the earlier triggers. Stage prompts are labelled instrument-test only (each line 5). The RQ2 secondary outcome includes responsibility wording without named harm (`04_methodology.tex:1858–1860`), while codebook v5:165–169 and stage2:6,21 restrict responsibility stance to named harms.

**Minimum fix:** make a versioned instrument bundle matching the chosen method: codebook, stage schemas/routing, human-blind sheets, sample/weight manifest, app-decision review form and walkthrough rating sheet. Define responsibility-without-harm as a separate code if retained; do not silently re-use a harm-conditioned stance. Identify a single authoritative manifest and update navigation. Preserve old versions as historical.

**Needs actual work:** run the new bundle on the real pilot. A consistency edit is necessary now, but it does not constitute validation.

nodes.label: M6 — Post-validation merging and selective reliability statistics can change the frozen target (moderate)
nodes.norm_label: m6 — post-validation merging and selective reliability statistics can change the frozen target (moderate)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1931–1933` freezes instruments and recodes affected material after changes; `1972–1978` computes α per axis/code “with enough positives” and then merges a code below a threshold. Axis codes are multilabel (`1601–1602`, `1672–1679`), and the validation sample deliberately enriches ambiguity (`1949–1955`). No representation/distance for axis α, weighted versus unweighted α, positive sufficiency rule, or independent revalidation after merging is specified.

**Minimum fix:** compute agreement on a declared representation (e.g., separate binary unit/code indicators, plus explicitly justified span/relationship agreement), state the effect of the enriched design and whether weighting is used, and retain raw prevalence/confusion tables. Distinguish unreliability from undefined/unstable α. Predefine code aggregation during development where possible. If evaluation triggers a substantive code change, freeze a new version, recode affected material and use fresh independent evaluation or label the revised result exploratory. Do not reuse a tuned validation set as untouched confirmation.

**Needs actual work:** agreement computation and, if rules change after validation, additional independent labels. Existing threshold prose cannot show that categories are reproducible.

nodes.label: M7 — Applicability uncertainty is displayed but not yet propagated coherently to the reported gap (moderate)
nodes.norm_label: m7 — applicability uncertainty is displayed but not yet propagated coherently to the reported gap (moderate)
nodes.rationale:
**Evidence:** `04_methodology.tex:1782–1799` derives applicability partly from provider disclosures and applies strong assumptions to external events. `1845–1853` alternates “each harm's” app denominator, pathway denominators and two calculations with uncertain pathways. It does not specify what enters the numerator when uncertain pathways are included. `1806` counts a named harm for every pathway in its category, while codebook v5:248 requires matching the pathway's data.

**Why it matters:** disclosure supplies both the opportunity to classify a pathway as applicable and the communication outcome. Transparent providers can have more known pathways, while sparse providers have more uncertain ones. Adding uncertain pathways only to the denominator is not a general bound unless their unknown communication/applicability states are handled explicitly. Broad harm language can also cover numerous pathways by the tree's construction rather than by provider-specific evidence.

**Minimum fix:** define one primary weighting unit (equal provider/app, equal pathway, or a stated within-provider average); keep alternative units as sensitivity analyses. Write the numerator as well as the denominator for uncertain-case scenarios and label them sensitivity scenarios rather than identification bounds unless bounds are derived. Specify matching by data/actor/scope for broad harm mentions. Report documented versus argued pathways and state external-event assumptions separately so readers can see whether those modeling choices drive the gap.

**Needs actual work:** second-person appraisal of applicability and source support, and sensitivity outputs once real records exist. Definitional ambiguity is repairable in prose; sensitivity results cannot be invented in advance.

**Severity:** Major for a final empirical submission; expected incompleteness for a pre-pilot plan.

**Evidence anchor:** `text: methodology L1392–1393, "the platform rule for apps listed in both stores"; L1495–1496, "The pilot fixes starting states, search boundaries, time limits and completion criteria"; L1447–1448; L1919–1933; protocol L23–34.`

nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Major.

**Evidence anchor:** `text: methodology L1335–1336, "A supplement for another region is recorded but not coded"; L1344–1345, "English text is primary for every source"; L1350–1352; D07 L13–19.`

**Finding:** The draft excludes out-of-region supplements, but does not explicitly state how the primary English document is checked for applicability to a German-market user. An English US policy and a German EU policy may differ because their audiences differ, rather than because one translation omitted text. Arora's MAPP-59 pairs are expressly semi-parallel policies aimed at US versus German users (PDF p.1); §§6–6.1 discuss jurisdiction-specific provisions. A difference log alone cannot make a US-only policy an applicable primary representation for German users. This is a possible failure mode, not a finding that any sampled provider has such a mismatch.

**Minimum fix:** Preserve English first, but require the capture record to identify product, policy scope, territorial audience, and applicable regional sections for every primary policy. Prefer an English version demonstrably covering German/EEA users. If only an out-of-region English document exists, keep its audience label explicit and document the treatment of the applicable German policy under the existing fallback/supervisor decision; do not silently equate language availability with market applicability. Keep comparisons within matching jurisdiction and scope.

**Confidence:** High about the missing explicit check and Arora's source population; moderate about practical frequency because no sampled policy pairs were audited here.

nodes.label: W3 — Composite control tasks can hide partial success and different protections
nodes.norm_label: w3 — composite control tasks can hide partial success and different protections
nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Major for comparative task-outcome claims.

**Evidence anchor:** `text: methodology L1434, "Turn off sharing with third parties"; L1436, "Delete the account and the data"; L1486–1492; protocol L63–79.`

**Finding:** The endpoint record is a strong improvement, but the fixed task labels still combine distinct goals. Disabling personalized advertising, analytics or one vendor is not the same control as stopping all third-party sharing. Removing a local history, an account, a server copy and community contributions are likewise different scopes. A single completed/not-found/unsupported/barrier outcome could conceal those differences unless the pilot's completion criteria explicitly preserve them. Malki directly illustrates separate controls, contradictory sharing preferences, account-only deletion and distinct device/cloud deletion (§§4.3.2,4.3.4; PDF pp.10–12).

**Minimum fix:** Keep T1–T7, but give T5/T6/T7 structured subgoal fields: data/recipient or purpose, account/local/server scope, offered action, requested versus interface-confirmed endpoint, and any partial or unresolved remainder. Apply the four neutral outcome categories per relevant subgoal or define a transparent task-level aggregation rule. Do not require backend verification. For apps without accounts, explicitly distinguish data deletion from an inapplicable account-deletion subgoal. Freeze these rules before main collection and report scoped outcomes.

**Confidence:** High that task labels are composite; moderate that they would cause actual miscoding, because a sufficiently detailed pilot protocol could resolve the ambiguity.

nodes.label: W4 — The bilingual difference log is promised without a complete operating rule
nodes.norm_label: w4 — the bilingual difference log is promised without a complete operating rule
nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Major if used to claim the language cost has been measured; otherwise Minor drafting incompleteness.

**Evidence anchor:** `text: methodology L1345–1346, "both are captured and their differences logged"; L1353–1355, "If the pilot shows"; L1444–1446; L2093–2095, "the difference log measures how much this matters"; protocol L26–28, L151–163.`

**Finding:** The current text does not specify the comparison unit, reviewer, classification of a material difference, completeness check, or denominator for the log. The extra-coding trigger is stated for a source noticed in the pilot; the treatment of a German-only harm/protection passage first noticed during main collection is not explicit. For UI, a counterpart pass after T5 changes or account deletion can also yield a different state rather than a language difference unless matched-state capture is specified. The protocol sensibly says all evidence precedes T7, but it does not explain how counterpart capture is placed relative to state-changing tasks.

**Minimum fix:** Add a compact template/rule: source/screen pair, jurisdiction and version, matched account/consent/setting state, English and German spans, changed node or claim scope, and reviewer judgment. State whether the same source-level trigger for extra German coding applies throughout collection, with logged instrument changes and recoding when necessary. Capture counterparts before destructive/state-changing actions or document a controlled equivalent state. Report pairs compared, unavailable counterparts and materially different pairs. Until such a procedure exists, say the log documents observed differences, not that it measures the full effect of language choice.

**Confidence:** High for the textual omissions; moderate for UI feasibility, which the real pilot must establish. This finding does not recommend replacing English-first.

nodes.label: W5 — The novice is specified by app experience, but the privacy goal is still researcher-supplied
nodes.norm_label: w5 — the novice is specified by app experience, but the privacy goal is still researcher-supplied
nodes.rationale:
**Severity:** Minor with the current cautious claim boundary; Major only if results generalize to ordinary user success or spontaneous discovery.

**Evidence anchor:** `text: methodology L1397–1400, "no prior knowledge of this app or its privacy policy"; L1409–1417; L1476–1483; protocol L38–53.`

**Finding:** A first-time platform user can still vary greatly in privacy vocabulary, literacy, language fluency and knowledge of third-party sharing or inference. The tasks ask a novice to pursue concepts derived from an expert harm tree. Without an explicit lay scenario and supplied knowledge, a Q1 judgment about trying the right effect risks importing the analyst's privacy expertise into the imagined user. Malki's app novice is not evidence of no technical training or no privacy knowledge. This does not require recruiting users.

**Minimum fix:** Freeze a short lay scenario and assumed privacy knowledge/language competence for each task, clarify that the user is assumed to have been given that goal, and rate Q1–Q4 conditional on those assumptions. Keep findings about likely obstacles for that persona rather than prevalence of concern or spontaneous discovery. List low-literacy, disabled and coercively monitored users as outside the tested persona where relevant, without claiming their experiences were studied.

**Confidence:** High on the distinction between task instruction and spontaneous user goals; moderate on how much the planned pilot will already address it.

nodes.label: malki2024exploring: Exploring Privacy Practices of Female mHealth Apps in a                Post-Roe World
nodes.description: Bibliography entry; verify claims in the original paper. Abstract (verbatim from the PDF): Mobile apps which support women’s health have developed rapidly alongside the increasing de-stigmatisation of female reproductive wellbeing. However, the ubiquity of these apps has advanced the practice of intimate surveillance and the commodification of sensitive user data. While the overturning of Roe v. Wade has prompted reflection on the privacy and safety implications of female mobile health (mHealth) apps, the privacy practices of these apps have yet to be thoroughly examined in a post-Roe world. We investigated the privacy practices of 20 popular female mHealth apps, combining a thematic analysis of Data safety sections and privacy policies with a privacy-focused usability inspection. Our findings revealed problematic practices, including inconsistencies across privacy policy content and privacy-related app features, flawed consent and data deletion mechanisms, and covert gatherin…
